title: Polar: A Benchmark for Evaluating Political Bias in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2606.12922v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Political bias in large language models (LLMs) is increasingly significant, but difficult to measure reproducibly across political and linguistic contexts. We introduce Polar, a 4,026-instance multiple-choice benchmark that measures political bias through option-level likelihoods rather than prompt-based generation. Polar covers two ideological axes and eight issue categories derived from the Manifesto Project, and evaluates models in parallel across U.S. and South Korean political contexts. Across 38 LLMs, measured bias varies systematically with political context, issue category, model group, and presentation language. All models lean left-progressive on U.S. political content, but show more centered and mixed patterns on South Korean content. Translation experiments further show that presentation language alone can shift measured bias. These findings highlight the need for multilingual and cross-contextual evaluation of political

translated_title: Polar：一个用于评估大语言模型政治偏见的基准
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）中的政治偏见日益重要，但在不同的政治和语言环境下难以进行可复现的测量。我们提出了Polar，一个包含4,026个实例的多项选择基准，它通过选项级别的似然概率而非基于提示的生成方式来测量政治偏见。Polar涵盖源自宣言项目的两个意识形态维度和八个议题类别，并在美国和韩国的政治语境中并行评估模型。在38个大语言模型上的实验显示，测得的偏见随政治语境、议题类别、模型组和展示语言的变化而系统性变化。所有模型在美国政治内容上都倾向于左翼进步立场，但在韩国内容上则表现出更为居中和混合的模式。翻译实验进一步表明，仅展示语言本身就能改变测得的偏见。这些发现凸显了开展多语言、跨语境政治偏见评估的必要性。
tldr: 提出了Polar基准，通过选项级似然概率在美韩两种政治语境和八个议题类别上测量38个大语言模型的政治偏见，发现所有模型在美国内容上均偏向左翼进步立场，且展示语言本身即可改变测得的偏见结果。
en_tdlr: Polar is a 4,026-instance multiple-choice benchmark that measures political bias in 38 LLMs via option-level likelihoods across U.S. and South Korean contexts, finding that all models lean left-progressive on U.S. content and that presentation language alone can shift measured bias.
